_comment: A ratchet, not an amnesty. `axe.spec.ts` fails on any serious or critical
violation not listed here, so adding a row is a deliberate act that shows
up in review. Rows may be deleted freely.
`allow` suppresses a rule on named pages — use sparingly, it blinds that
`exclude` removes specific elements from the scan. Prefer it: it is the
narrow tool, and every entry has to say what was measured and why the

exclude.reason: axe false positive, measured. It reports 'contrast 1.05:1, foreground #0c0a09 on background #121217' for the white CTA on the dark plate — reading the plate's colour instead of the button's. The element's own computed style is backgroundColor rgb(255,255,255), opacity 1, colour stone-950: about 18:1. Every ancestor is opacity 1, so this is not the mid-animation artefact (that one was real and is fixed by the reducedMotion setting in the spec). Most likely axe's background resolution and the button's `bg-clip-padding` + transparent border. Re-check on the next axe-core upgrade.
